### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A14, A15 and A20 each appeared in about 47 in 100 traces (94 of 200); in the later window each appears in about 995 in 1000 traces (199 of 200), still at most once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- In the earlier window, the segment from A36 to A21 had two forms: about 47 in 100 traces ran A36 → A14 → A20 → A15 → A21 (A36's outgoing transitions led to A14 in about 47 in 100 cases, and A36 reached A21 four steps later), while the remaining ~53 in 100 went directly from A36 to A21 in a single step. [DIR001, LAG001, REL003, REL008, REL012]
- In the later window the through-route is near-universal: A36's outgoing transitions lead to A14 in about 995 in 1000 cases, A36 reaches A21 at a distance of four steps in about 995 in 1000 traces, and the direct one-step A36 → A21 remains in only about 1 in 200 traces. [DIR001, LAG001]
- The block's internal order is fixed and unchanged: A36 before A14, A14 before A20, A20 before A15, and the block before A21 in essentially every trace containing them, in both windows; A36 and A21 themselves occur in all traces in both windows. [REL004, REL002, REL007, REL001, REL003, REL008, REL012, DIR001]
- Relative positions within the trace shifted slightly and consistently with this: A36 now sits a little earlier (mean relative position about 0.33 → 0.30) and A21 a little later (about 0.41 → 0.43). [POS002, POS001]
- A40 appears in about 60 in 100 traces in both windows, but in the earlier window it also occurred without A14 (about 33 in 100 traces), whereas in the later window it never does; A37 occurs in all traces in both windows and keeps an unfixed order relative to the block, somewhat more interleaved in the later window (A14/A37 interleaved in about 17 vs 45 in 100 traces). [REL006, REL011, REL015, REL005, REL010, REL014]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the block A14 → A20 → A15, sitting between A36 and A21, changed from optional to executed in nearly every case: in the earlier window about 47 in 100 traces ran A36 → A14 → A20 → A15 → A21 while the rest skipped the block and passed directly from A36 to A21, whereas in the later window about 995 in 1000 traces run the block and the direct A36 → A21 step survives in only about 1 in 200 traces. Supporting signs: the participation of all three block activities rose in step (about 47% to about 99.5%, backed by 94–199 traces per window); relational evidence places A36 before A14, A14 before A20, A20 before A15 and the block before A21 in about 995 in 1000 later traces; A36's successor shifted from A21 (about 53% of outgoing transitions) to A14 (about 99.5%); and the A36-to-A21 distance moved from one step (about 53 in 100 traces) to four steps (about 995 in 1000). The pattern is unlikely to arise from sampling alone: 22 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.41 expected by chance, and every item's difference exceeds 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data. One competing explanation cannot be ruled out: the direct A36 → A21 route still appears in about 1 in 200 later traces, so the evidence cannot tell whether the skip option was removed or is only rarely taken, nor whether the routing itself changed or only the mix of cases reaching this segment. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, LAG001, REL002, REL004, REL007, REL008]

Other differences: A40's participation is stable (about 60 in 100 traces in both windows), but it no longer occurs outside block traces — in the earlier window it appeared without A14 in about 33 in 100 traces, in the later window never — and A37, present throughout, keeps an unfixed order relative to the block with more interleaving in the later window (A14/A37 interleaved in about 17 vs 45 in 100 traces); A36 and A21 also sit slightly earlier and later in the trace, respectively. [REL006, REL011, REL015, REL005, REL010, REL014, POS002, POS001]
